incident-bot: ALERT: p99 decode latency spike detected across us-west-2 serving pool (service: hosted-gpt-stream). SLO breach potential. Automated mitigations triggered: scale-up attempt and fallback routing. root_ts=1768765432

maya (eng-oncall): saw this on the dashboard, p95 up ~3x, p99 ~6x. streaming sessions timing out at tail tokens. customers -> live chat / embeddings pipelines affected.

raj (eng-runtime): any recent kernel or compiler changes deployed to us-west-2 within last 2 hours?

deploy-bot: Deployment: runtime-kernel-v2.9.1 rolled to us-west-2 at 1768763000 by ci/cd (canary->stable). Change: flashattn 2.0.3 + new compile flag -O3 -fno-strict-aliasing -DTRT_OPT=1

elena (eng-sre): correlation looks strong with the v2.9.1 rollout window. paging events increased concurrently, KV cache eviction rate spiking. p99 tail sits at decode step, streaming stalls mid-response.

maya (eng-oncall): oncall runbook check: 1) verify customer impact, 2) scale and isolate, 3) rollback if needed. I'm paging runtime team. @raj can you triage kernel regressions?

raj (eng-runtime): looking now. attaching quick profiler snippet and qps overlays. initial hunch: new flashattn kernel changes change memory pattern -> higher register pressure -> occasional L2 thrash causing paging for long sequences.

doug (support): we already have 3 enterprise customers reporting degraded streaming experience (partial responses, reconnects). Two opened P1 tickets.

maya (eng-oncall): immediate mitigation: enable fallback routing to dedicated-compat model group (slower model but stable kernels). Initiating now.

deploy-bot: Fallback routing policy applied to 20% of traffic for hosted-gpt-stream in us-west-2 at 1768765480.

elena (eng-sre): also increasing hot pool size + temporarily raising memory limit on decode workers to reduce page faults. Doing a gradual scale now.

raj (eng-runtime): collecting kernel logs from a failing pod. snippet below:

```
[2026-03-15T14:30:12Z] kernel: flashattn_opt: allocated 2.1GB workspace
[2026-03-15T14:30:12Z] runtime: decode: kv-cache miss spike, eviction count=4321
[2026-03-15T14:30:13Z] perf: l2-misses +48% over baseline
[2026-03-15T14:30:15Z] oom_kill: none
[2026-03-15T14:30:17Z] streaming: stall at token 412 of 1024, wait-for-kernel 112ms
```

raj (eng-runtime): compile flags from the build:

```
CXXFLAGS="-O3 -march=native -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti -funroll-loops -fomit-frame-pointer -fno-strict-aliasing -DTRT_OPT=1"
LDFLAGS="-Wl,-O1"
```

maya (eng-oncall): any quick rollback plan? how fast to revert to v2.9.0?

raj (eng-runtime): we can rollback canary -> stable in place, but stable already at 80% traffic. If we flip the routing to v2.9.0, pods will gradually be replaced. Estimate ~4-6 minutes to reach 90% traffic. Immediate patch: disable the flashattn kernel switch via runtime config to force legacy kernel selection (hotfix flag). That should be <2min if config pushes succeed.

elena (eng-sre): I'm leaning to config toggle first to avoid full rollback chaos. Doing toggle: runtime.feature.flashattn=false to the us-west-2 config set. Pushing now.

deploy-bot: Config update applied at 1768765530: runtime.feature.flashattn=false -> rollout to us-west-2 clusters (gradual 30s waves).

raj (eng-runtime): seeing immediate improvement on a few pods: p99 reduced from 1.2s -> 420ms on affected instances. KV eviction rate dropping.

doug (support): updating customer tickets: pinging affected customers that we have mitigation in place and are monitoring.

maya (eng-oncall): good. action items: 1) keep fallback routing active until stable p99 < baseline + 10% for 15m; 2) follow up with a full rollback if config toggle doesn't hold; 3) collect core dumps / perf traces from affected kernels for root cause; 4) schedule a safety revert for the build with the flashattn flags.

raj (eng-runtime): collecting traces now. request: eng-sre please preserve the affected worker images and disk caches for postmortem. Also we should capture the exact sequence length distribution that triggered the tail.

elena (eng-sre): snapshotting nodes (preserve-logs=true) and disabling auto-reclaim for 30m.

maya (eng-oncall): customer impact note for ops/comms: p95 peaked ~350ms -> 1.1s, p99 peaked ~900ms -> 2.8s depending on sequence length. Several streaming sessions experienced stalls >5s before auto-retry. We'll draft a status update if this persists.

doug (support): I pushed a proactive message to the three P1 customers and offered a temporary route to dedicated capacity. Two accepted the mitigate route.

raj (eng-runtime): for the postmortem: candidates: 1) flashattn memory layout changes + compile optimizations (O3 + fomit-frame-pointer) exposing register spill/prefetch regressions; 2) linker LTO/ldflags interaction causing less locality; 3) TRTagent optimizer flag (-DTRT_OPT=1) toggling a fast-path. Need to reproduce with long-seq load test.

maya (eng-oncall): timeline so far recorded. Next handoff: I'll leave this as active and hand to night oncall in 45m unless stabilized. @elena please prepare escalation note for infra if we need node-level kernel rollback.

elena (eng-sre): noted. I'll prepare a kernel-rollback playbook and the node snapshot list.

raj (eng-runtime): quick mitigation retrospective: prefer config toggle + routing fallback as primary mitigation for kernel regressions. We should also add a preflight long-seq run for kernel/flashattn builds. Filing a follow-up RFC.

maya (eng-oncall): thanks team. I'll update thread if anything changes. current state: mitigation applied, metrics trending back toward baseline but under observation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation succeeded; p99 decreased to 1.1x baseline over 10m window. Monitoring continues.

maya (eng-oncall): handoff note for next oncall: watch p95/p99, streaming stall rate, KV cache eviction, and keep fallback at 20% until stable for 15m. If recurrence, escalate to full rollback.

(End of thread)
